To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anomalous dimension of the WZNW model determines the scaling of isospin correlations in the chiral limit and that the anomalous dimensions for the chiral limit is the same as for the massive case.

the (1+2) WZNW scaling of the chiral condensates can be extended to the (1+3) case, and that the resulting anomalous dimension can be used to describe correlations of pion clusters produced in the central rapidity of a nuclear collision.

in a (1+1)-dimensional effective theory of chiral order parameter, in certain regions of phase space, correlations of this order parameter are described in the scaling regime by the fixed point solution of the (1/1)-dimensional WZNW model with anomalous dimension that determines the scaling of the probability of observing a cluster of correlated pions with the cluster size in rapidity.

in the region of rapidity corresponding to a fixed point of the WZNW model, the chiral condensat is disoriented.
